Maya Chen: Heads-up: legal asked us to reconcile language around 'retention' vs 'data retention TTL' in the SOC2 audit-log docs. Which term do we settle on?
Jules Park: Use 'retention period' in user-facing docs. Keep 'TTL' only in infra/SDK notes.
DevSecOps Bot: Reminder: security wants a line about exports possibly containing pseudonymized IDs and a KMS mention.
Chris Patel: Suggested sentence: 'Audit exports may include pseudonymized identifiers; customers are responsible for downstream de-identification for regulated workflows.'
Nisha Verma: +1. Also call out default windows: hosted audit logs: 90 days; privileged access logs: 180 days. Make clear enterprise/Dedicated can have custom SLAs.
Maya Chen: I'll add a short example block and minimal SDK snippets (curl + python). Proposed curl snippet: ```bash
curl -X POST 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/audit/exports 
  -d '{"scope":"tenant","before":"YYYY-MM-DDT00:00:00Z"}'
```
Jules Park: please avoid real future dates in docs; use the ISO placeholder as above and mention UTC.
Maya Chen: Python snippet ready: ```python
from redwood import AuditClient
client = AuditClient(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_KEY'))
client.export(scope='tenant', before='YYYY-MM-DDT00:00:00Z')
```
Chris Patel: Also add: 'Export files are encrypted at rest using customer-managed or Redwood-managed keys; see KMS docs for rotation.'
Nisha Verma: Legal and security both ok with that wording.
Maya Chen: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/5302 — requesting final review for phrasing and link checks.
DevSecOps Bot: Link check passed. Docs build: success.
Chris Patel: LGTM. Approved.
Maya Chen: Merged to main and added backport tasks for enterprise/private. Thanks everyone :sparkles:
